----------
howdy, it’s Barsee again.

happy friday, AI family, and welcome back to AI Valley.

**here are the biggest things worth knowing today:**

* Qwen just got a seriously capable uncensored version

* Slack launched Slack Code

* Anthropic wants to beat SpaceX’s IPO record

* Plus trending AI tools, posts, and resources

Let’s _dive_ into the Valley of AI…


----------

----------
#### **FITNEXA**

## [Most Earbuds Weren’t Made for Bed](https://go.fitnexa.com/DPo07i)

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/57386ca0-3b1f-4e0d-8055-619dfa6a6fd6/20251021-114822__1___1_.png?t=1787059367)
Follow image link: (https://go.fitnexa.com/DPo07i)
Caption: Courtesy Fitnexa

Most wireless earbuds are designed for commuting, working out, or taking calls. Sleeping in them is kind of an afterthought.

SomniPods 3 take the opposite approach.

They’re 9.9mm thin, weigh 3.3g each, and are shaped to sit more comfortably when your ear is against a pillow. They also combine Hybrid ANC, passive isolation, and sound masking to help with the kind of noise that suddenly feels very loud at 2 a.m.

It’s one of those products that makes more sense once you realize how oddly specific the problem is.

If you already sleep with earbuds, or have tried and hated it, SomniPods 3 are probably much closer to what you were looking for.

[See SomniPods 3](https://go.fitnexa.com/DPo07i)

~_*This is sponsored_~


----------

----------
#### **THROUGH THE VALLEY**

Tweet:  (https://twitter.com/gregpr07/status/2089897646739894354?s=20)

**1/ Qwen just got a seriously capable uncensored version** - independent teams including OrcaRouter and AEON-7 used a technique called “abliteration” to remove much of [Alibaba’s Qwen3.8-27B’s](https://huggingface.co/orcarouter/Qwen3.8-27B-Uncensored-MLX?utm_source=chatgpt.com) refusal behavior without stripping away its core intelligence. It’s not an official Alibaba release, but a community modification that keeps the original model’s coding, agentic, vision, reasoning, and 262K-token context capabilities, while being small enough to run locally on consumer hardware. ([watch the demo](https://x.com/gregpr07/status/2089897646739894354?s=20))

The wild part is that this isn’t a tiny jailbreak model... Qwen3.8-27B is a 27B open-weight model with capabilities that can compete with much larger systems, and the uncensored versions can run directly on [Apple Silicon Macs](https://x.com/akshen121/status/2090044678158860771?s=20) or consumer GPUs. The model also retains its thinking mode, so users can control how much reasoning it does before answering.

And this is where things get controversial... researchers and red-teamers can use it for security testing without cloud-based safety filters getting in the way, but the same capabilities can also be used for harmful or illegal requests.

**2/ Slack launched Slack Code** - it gives teams [dedicated channels](https://x.com/Benioff/status/2090240159115853956?s=20) where humans and AI agents can build software together. Tag Claude, ChatGPT, Devin or Copilot and it spins up a code channel with the plan, conversation, diffs and live preview all in one place. Slack Code is free on every plan, though the agents themselves are separately paid. ([learn more here](https://x.com/SlackHQ/status/2090415566351659267))

Slack is becoming the new agent workspace... The interesting bit is that everyone can watch the agent work, review its diffs, give feedback and approve changes before they ship. Anyone can also pause or redirect an agent, while production merges require human sign-off. So it’s more like “your whole team builds with AI in the same room.”

And coding probably isn’t the end game. Slack says the same infrastructure could eventually let custom agents handle things like marketing campaigns, legal reviews and other workflows.

**3/ Anthropic wants to beat SpaceX’s IPO record** - the Claude maker is reportedly preparing to [match or top](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-20/anthropic-expects-to-match-spacex-s-record-ipo-size-or-top-it?accessToken=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzb3VyY2UiOiJTdWJzY3JpYmVyR2lmdGVkQXJ0aWNsZSIsImlhdCI6MTc4NzI5NzA2MCwiZXhwIjoxNzg3OTAxODYwLCJhcnRpY2xlSWQiOiJUSzBUVktLSzNOWUMwMCIsImJjb25uZWN0SWQiOiI2NTc1NjkyN0UwMkM0N0MwQkQ0MDNEQTJGMEUyNzIyMyJ9.OxE678o5_5twVs_xmvCzAFwLomwkkT77ZbpvHnLXzco&utm_source=tldrnewsletter&leadSource=article-gifting) SpaceX’s record $75B IPO, with a public filing potentially coming by the end of this month. SpaceX’s IPO raised a record $86.2 billion, which means Anthropic could raise close to $100 billion. Anthropic was valued at $965B in its latest funding round, and its revenue is absolutely flying: Q2 revenue topped $11.5B, up from just $787M a year earlier.

The spending is wild too... Anthropic reportedly lost almost $42B in 2025, roughly 5x more than the year before.

Anthropic could also beat OpenAI to the public markets... both companies have confidentially filed, but OpenAI is reportedly looking at 2027. If Anthropic actually pulls off a $75B+ IPO, it would instantly become one of the biggest IPOs ever and push 2026 toward becoming the biggest year for US IPOs on record. Anthropic is expected to IPO by the end of 2026.


----------

----------
# TRENDING TOOLS


--------------------
* [LongCat-Avatar](https://x.com/0xJokker/status/2090441836317811176?s=20) - a foundational video generation model with 13.6B parameters, delivering strong performance across Text-to-Video, Image-to-Video, and Video-Continuation generation

* [Replit Free Mode](https://replit.com/blog/replit-introduces-free-mode) - lets users create 30x more with OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Luna without using credits for everyday tasks

* [Grok Build](https://x.ai/news/grok-build-for-everyone) - turns a single prompt into a published app, game, website, or dashboard, complete with its own domain

* [Exa](https://x.com/ExaAILabs/status/2090472683758841932) - now available as a plug-in in Codex and ChatGPT


----------

----------
# WHAT I'M CONSUMING


--------------------
* [Claude Academy is now live](https://academy.claude.com/). The courses and tutorials are free and open to anyone

# THE VALLEY GEMS


--------------------

----------------------------------------




COUNTERPOINT

WRITING ISN’T THE ONLY WAY TO THINK

Head of tech consulting Mike Taylor https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiSW4gRGVmZW5zZSBvZiBBSSBXcml0aW5nIiwicG9zdF9pZCI6NDQ0NiwicG9zdF90eXBlIjoicG9zdCIsInVybCI6Imh0dHBzOi8vZXZlcnkudG8vQG1pa2VfMjExNCIsInBvc2l0aW9uIjo2fQ== has regularly used AI in his writing. One of the most popular articles https://every. he’s published on Every was ghostwritten by Claude, as were most of the posts on his personal blog https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiSW4gRGVmZW5zZSBvZiBBSSBXcml0aW5nIiwicG9zdF9pZCI6NDQ0NiwicG9zdF90eXBlIjoicG9zdCIsInVybCI6Imh0dHBzOi8vd3d3LnNheGlmcmFnZS54eXovIiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjh9; he revises sections and makes structural edits, but he doesn’t generate the majority of the text himself.

This is the kind of admission that makes the internet foam at the mouth. People really hate AI writing. The most common objection is simple: Writing is thinking https://every.. If you outsource the drafting process to an LLM, you have outsourced the reasoning and judgment critical to forming an original idea. Of course the result is slop. Stop wasting everyone’s time. But it’s not always that simple: Having something compelling to say doesn’t make you a great writer, just as being a great writer doesn’t necessarily mean you have something compelling to say.

Mike is the first to admit he’s more of a doer than a writer. He’s out in the world, teaching executives how to use AI at their organizations to get work done. He also tests new models before they are released and is currently building an evaluation set to automate CEO Dan Shipper https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiSW4gRGVmZW5zZSBvZiBBSSBXcml0aW5nIiwicG9zdF9pZCI6NDQ0NiwicG9zdF90eXBlIjoicG9zdCIsInVybCI6Imh0dHBzOi8vZXZlcnkudG8vQGRhbnNoaXBwZXIiLCJwb3NpdGlvbiI6MTB9’s judgment.

Mike would never prompt an AI to write about an A/B test he didn’t perform himself. “But if I’ve run the test, I think it’s completely valid for me to go to an AI and say, ‘I ran a test. Here’s what I did and how,’” he says. He’ll dictate everything, from setup to results, and then use AI to format it all into a post.

The process shrinks a full day of writing down to two hours and gets what he’s learned in front of more people more often. That—not beautiful prose—is the goal. (For the record, Mike also loathes posts where it’s clear the author didn’t bother to review what AI spat out; those two hours of his time include reading and revising.)

As a reader, he prioritizes functionality over style. “If you put this strict cap on it—‘You have to be a good writer to get your ideas out’—you miss almost all of the interesting things happening in the world,” he says.

https://every. general manager Kieran Klaassen has Mike’s back. (Screenshot courtesy of Laura Entis.)



----------------------------------------






https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiSW4gRGVmZW5zZSBvZiBBSSBXcml0aW5nIiwicG9zdF9pZCI6NDQ0NiwicG9zdF90eXBlIjoicG9zdCIsInVybCI6Imh0dHBzOi8vYnJpZWZocS5haS8_dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1ldmVyeVx1MDAyNnV0bV9tZWRpdW09bmV3c2xldHRlclx1MDAyNnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1icmllZl9xM18yMDI2XHUwMDI2dXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9cHJpbWFyeSIsInBvc2l0aW9uIjoxMn0=

CUSTOMERS CAN’T USE PROTOTYPES

PMs can build strong prototypes around a clear customer need, but a prototype isn’t a system. It doesn’t carry the constraints, tradeoffs, or paths engineering tried and rejected.

Brief closes that gap. It keeps customer evidence, product decisions, and engineering constraints attached to work. So prototypes that reach engineering already reflect what the codebase can do.

Learn more about Brief https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiSW4gRGVmZW5zZSBvZiBBSSBXcml0aW5nIiwicG9zdF9pZCI6NDQ0NiwicG9zdF90eXBlIjoicG9zdCIsInVybCI6Imh0dHBzOi8vYnJpZWZocS5haS8_dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1ldmVyeVx1MDAyNnV0bV9tZWRpdW09bmV3c2xldHRlclx1MDAyNnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1icmllZl9xM18yMDI2XHUwMDI2dXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9cHJpbWFyeVx1MDAyNnNvdXJjZT1wb3N0X2J1dHRvbiIsInBvc2l0aW9uIjoxM30=

----------
howdy, it’s Barsee again.

happy thursday, AI family, and welcome back to AI Valley.

**here are the biggest things worth knowing today:**

* OpenAI is slowing down

* Stripe says we’ve entered the singularity

* A robot learned a new task from one 3-second example

* Plus trending AI tools, posts, and resources

Let’s _dive_ into the Valley of AI…


----------

----------
#### **WISPR FLOW**

## [Everywhere workflow (one voice layer across tools)](https://ref.wisprflow.ai/aivalley)

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/a623e39d-51fe-4203-bd39-d4235979fc6d/Newsletters_Image_1920x1080__7___6_.png?t=1787233833)
Caption: Courtesy: Wispr Flow

Flow is a voice layer that works anywhere you type. Use it to respond in Slack, write docs, craft emails, or prompt an AI assistant without switching tools or copy/pasting. It's the fastest way to get high-quality text into your workflow, whether you're drafting, editing, or ideating.

[**Try Flow Free**](https://ref.wisprflow.ai/aivalley)

~_*This is sponsored_~


----------

----------
#### **THROUGH THE VALLEY**

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/e22e19dc-ec89-47c8-bd0c-166bad100918/substack-post-media.s3.amazonaws__100___1_.png?t=1787234318)
Caption: Courtesy: Sam Altman

**1/ OpenAI is slowing down its most powerful models** - the company has [paused](https://openai.com/index/pacing-model-development-cyber-capabilities/) some frontier reinforcement learning training for two weeks and put its largest planned run on hold while it runs smaller evaluations and strengthens safety systems. The move comes after the Hugging Face breach and concerns that its upcoming Astra models may have crossed a “critical” threshold for cyber capabilities. OpenAI [says](https://x.com/alexeheath/status/2089777725385109784?s=20) its models are showing “various degrees of misalignment” as they get more capable.

OpenAI’s financials are also getting uglier... Revenue grew just 18% from Q1 to Q2, reaching $6.7B (vs Anthropic’s $11.6B), while losses jumped by $3B to $12.3B. That’s not exactly the kind of chart you want to see right before an IPO, especially as Anthropic’s revenue reportedly grew much faster during the same period.

**2/ Stripe says we’ve entered the singularity** - in a [letter](https://s3.documentcloud.org/documents/28565866/stripes-august-2026-investor-letter.pdf) to investors, Stripe said it considers January 1 the beginning of a new phase marked by accelerating AI, firm creation, and economic change. Their goal now is to help AI spread across the economy while building the financial infrastructure for agents. Oh, and as we covered in our last newsletter, they recently [acquired](https://www.theaivalley.com/p/stripe-acquires-openrouter-for-7b) OpenRouter, their largest-ever acquisition. Its token usage is compounding at 9% per week YTD.

Stripe also thinks “intelligence capital” is becoming a thing. The idea is that businesses will need to manage AI tokens the way they manage financial capital: which model should handle a task, how much should it cost, and what’s the return? OpenRouter fits neatly into this, giving developers a way to route requests across different models and providers.


----------

----------
#### **PEAK OF THE DAY**

## **A robot learned a new task from one 3-second example**

Youtube: Introducing GEN-1.5, a one-shot learner (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1cllCVK-9lo)

Robots can now learn some new physical tasks just by watching someone do them once.

Generalist’s new [GEN-1.5](https://generalistai.com/blog/gen-1.5?utm_source=www.theneurondaily.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=the-actual-chatgpt-3-moment-for-robotics-one-shot-learning) can watch a 3–12 second demonstration and immediately try the task itself. No fine-tuning. No gradient updates. Generalist calls this “physical prompting.”

Across 10 tasks, one demonstration produced a 59% average success rate. With 10 gradient steps on five minutes of data, that rose to 83%.

The model can also combine two demonstrations into a longer task, learn from simulated demonstrations and perform them on a real robot, and in some cases watch a human do something with their own hands and copy it.

Previous robot models could require tens of thousands of gradient steps to adapt to a new task. GEN-1.5 can do it in 1–10 steps, and Generalist says 10 steps changed its weights by less than 0.15%.

The one-shot capability itself isn’t quite continual learning. The model’s weights don’t change.

But that may be the more interesting result. GEN-1.5 has been pretrained on physical data for more than eight months, and the model appears to have learned enough general physical knowledge that a few seconds of new experience can actually be useful.

That’s a pretty big change from teaching a robot one task at a time.

The tasks here are still simple and the success rates are modest. But if robots can eventually learn new skills this quickly, remember them, and build on them without forgetting what they already know, the idea of robots learning directly from the world starts looking a lot more real.


----------

----------
# TRENDING TOOLS


--------------------
* [Claude](https://x.com/claudeai/status/2089806039088517356?s=20) - it can now send emails in Gmail and manage files in Google Drive

* [Zetik](https://www.zetik.com/) - an AI chief of staff that runs an agentic intelligence cycle to collect, filter, analyze, and brief you across multiple sources

* [Open Bot](https://x.com/ataiiam/status/2090125716767773120?s=20) - an open-source Grok bot that works with any agent harness, built for real-world companies

* [Harvey II](https://www.harvey.ai/blog/introducing-harvey-ii) - makes legal work more efficient by giving AI agents context, memory, and preferences from previous tasks, cutting down repetitive setup

* [Okara AI CMO v2](https://okara.ai/) - drop in your website, and it deploys a team of fast, smart agents to help drive traffic and acquire users

----------------------------------------


INSIDE EVERY

THE AGENTS BEHIND THE CURTAIN

Naveen Naidu https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiQW4gRW5naW5lZXJpbmcgVGVhbSBmb3IgdGhlIENvc3Qgb2YgQ29kZXgiLCJwb3N0X2lkIjo0NDQ1LCJwb3N0X3R5cGUiOiJwb3N0IiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9ldmVyeS50by9AbmF2ZWVuXzY4MDQiLCJwb3NpdGlvbiI6N30= is the one-man shop behind Monologue https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiQW4gRW5naW5lZXJpbmcgVGVhbSBmb3IgdGhlIENvc3Qgb2YgQ29kZXgiLCJwb3N0X2lkIjo0NDQ1LCJwb3N0X3R5cGUiOiJwb3N0IiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cubW9ub2xvZ3VlLnRvLz91dG1fc291cmNlPWV2ZXJ5d2Vic2l0ZSIsInBvc2l0aW9uIjo4fQ==, Every’s smart dictation app.

But Naveen no longer sees it that way—these days, his work feels more like managing a team of engineers.

The engineers just happen to be custom agents he built within Codex https://every.. On his roster: dedicated engineer agents across different disciplines, a customer support agent, and a growth strategist—all of which help maintain the Monologue website and app. Recently, a customer sent Naveen a glowing review that he wanted to feature on Monologue’s website. His customer support agent handed the review text to his web engineer agent, which added the testimonial.

Each agent is a Codex project, complete with a custom AGENTS.md file, skills, folders https://every., memory, codebases, and additional context that turns it into a specialist.

https://every.’s roster of Codex agents. (Image courtesy of Naveen Naidu.)




Until recently, those specialists worked in relative isolation. Naveen had to manually transfer Markdown files and instructions between projects whenever a task required contributions from multiple agents, like when the growth agent wrote copy for a new landing page built by the web agent. GPT-5.6 https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiQW4gRW5naW5lZXJpbmcgVGVhbSBmb3IgdGhlIENvc3Qgb2YgQ29kZXgiLCJwb3N0X2lkIjo0NDQ1LCJwb3N0X3R5cGUiOiJwb3N0IiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9ldmVyeS50by92aWJlLWNoZWNrL2dwdC01LTYiLCJwb3NpdGlvbiI6MTJ9 changed that equation; the model intuits context well enough that Naveen can instruct an agent to send over the relevant information to a separate project and kick off a new task there—the agent equivalent of having a direct report pass an assignment to a coworker.

https://every. a task is initiated by another project, Codex marks the text as “Sent by Codex from another chat.” (Screenshot courtesy of Naveen.)




When a Monologue user recently reported an echo in their audio, Naveen reviewed the conversation from his customer support project, which accesses tickets filed in Fin https://every.. He asked Codex to open a separate worktree thread (a task that operates in an isolated copy of the codebase), fix the bug, and create a pull request.

GPT-5.6 has made Naveen’s work faster and, although he remains Monologue’s only human engineer, more collaborative.

When intelligence is abundant and much of today’s execution can be automated, how will humans spend their time at work? What skills will matter? What kinds of companies will we build? Where will we find meaning, status, and purpose?

These are the most important questions of our time, and the places we usually turn for answers don’t have them yet.

But there’s a small group of people who do: The humans who are living with frontier models day in and day out, and applying them to their work and lives.

That has been our method at Every since the GPT-3 days, when it was not yet clear that LLMs were anything more than stochastic parrots. Over the years, we’ve argued that AI would let one person do work that once required a team, that knowledge workers would become managers of models, and that automation would paradoxically create more work for human experts.
